title: Attacks Through Permitted Operations
summary: Work through Attacks Through Permitted Operations.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Attacks Through Permitted Operations**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Agent Security, § Attacks Through Permitted Operations
blocks.md: The previous chapter closed on a disclosure that every boundary admitted, a diagnostic report that carried private fixture contents to an approved service because injected README text asked for them. The same attack needs no reporting tool at all. Return to the repository repair task (a later section). The repair agent is permitted to search external package registries and modify files within its local workspace, but it must never disclose private test fixtures.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Callable is not permitted matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Injection turns the runtime into a confused deputy with a legitimate identity, so authorization must judge this request within this task, not the function name, argument types, or endpoint allowlist.

questions.q: The section **Attacks Through Permitted Operations** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A defense is evaluated by system effects at the protected sink on whole eligible episodes, not by model text, and its overhead is priced in cost per accepted task.
An agent that combines access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and an external communication channel can be steered to exfiltrate, and removing any one leg breaks the attack path.
A quarantined reader keeps raw untrusted text out of the planner and typed handles keep untrusted bytes out of context, but a schema-valid field is still an untrusted claim, not evidence.
Injection turns the runtime into a confused deputy with a legitimate identity, so authorization must judge this request within this task, not the function name, argument types, or endpoint allowlist.
questions.hint: Re-read the excerpt and the section map: which idea is this section building toward?
